title: Finite terminal cartesian triangles extend relative boundaries
statement:
Use quasicategories, ordinary nerves, functor simplicial sets, Kan complexes and standard simplices of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and trivial Kan fibrations of [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. Fix a containing universe. For $n\geq0$, let $[n]$ be the ordered category $0<\cdots<n$, and let $T_n$ be the category with objects $(i,j)$ for $0\leq i\leq j\leq n$ and a unique arrow $(i,j)\to(i',j')$ when $i\leq i'\leq j'\leq j$. Its projection to $[n]^{\mathrm{op}}$ sends $(i,j)$ to $j$. Let $p:E\to N([n])^{\mathrm{op}}$ be a cartesian fibration and choose a terminal object $t_i\in E_i$ for each $i$, so every $\operatorname{Map}_{E_i}(x,t_i)$ is contractible.

Let $B_n\subseteq N(T_n)$ be the union of the images of $N(T_F)$ over all proper subsets $F\subsetneq\{0,\ldots,n\}$, where $T_F$ is the full subcategory on pairs with both indices in $F$. Thus $B_0=\varnothing$. For $X=N(T_n)$ or $B_n$, define a simplicial set $\mathcal L(X)$: its $m$-simplices are maps $F:X\times\Delta^m\to E$ over $N([n])^{\mathrm{op}}$, constant at $t_i$ on $\{(i,i)\}\times\Delta^m$ whenever this vertex belongs to $X$, and taking every edge $(i,j)\to(i,j')$ present in $X$ at every parameter vertex to a $p$-cartesian edge. Operators restrict the parameter simplex. Then restriction
$$\mathcal L(N(T_n))\longrightarrow\mathcal L(B_n)$$
is a trivial Kan fibration. Moreover $\mathcal L(N(T_n))$ and $\mathcal L(B_n)$ are nonempty contractible Kan complexes. The same assertion holds after pulling back a cartesian fibration along any simplex $N([n])^{\mathrm{op}}\to S$ of a quasicategory $S$. No cartesian transport is required to preserve terminal objects.

source.place: Agent finite-simplex extension lemma extracted from returned step 1; local terminal-boundary and cartesian-arrow extension argument. Motivation: Cisinski Section 5.6, not the statement of Proposition 5.6.9.

proof.text: We prove the boundary-lifting assertion slightly more generally for diagrams into a cartesian fibration $p:E\to S$ of quasicategories over a fixed simplex $\sigma:N([n])^{\mathrm{op}}\to S$. Cartesian edges are tested in $E$, and terminal diagonal values are chosen in the strict fibres $E_i=E_{\sigma(i)}$. The original assertion takes $S=N([n])^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $\sigma=\mathrm{id}$. For $n\geq1$, put $X=N(T_n)$ and delete $(n,n)$ to obtain $Y_n$. The vertices $(i,n)$ form a column simplex $C_n\cong\Delta^n$. Every chain containing $(n,n)$ lies in this column, since an arrow into $(n,n)$ forces the source's second coordinate to be $n$. Thus $X=Y_n\cup C_n$ and $Y_n\cap C_n$ is the face opposite the last vertex. Put $D_n=B_n\cap Y_n$. Every diagonal $(i,i)$ for $i<n$ belongs to $D_n$, using the proper singleton subset $\{i\}$.

source.place: Agent expansion of proof paragraph 2 through the finite-simplex terminal-comparison ancestry; marked lifting and terminal boundary extension, with all parameter boundaries fixed.

proof.text: Mark exactly the $p$-cartesian edges of $E$. Degenerate edges are cartesian: their inverse witnesses make them equivalences, and [lem-cbc-inner-fibration-equivalence-outer-horn-lift] fills every required final horn. We check the four generating families in [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus] for $E^\natural\to S^\sharp$. Family (i) lifts by innerness. Family (ii) for dimension at least two lifts by the defining final-horn property of a marked edge; in dimension one it is the existence of a cartesian edge with prescribed target. Family (iii) only asks that the long edge of a triangle with cartesian consecutive edges be cartesian. Take opposites in [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]: reversing simplex order exchanges initial and final horns, and the cited composition equivalence gives this conclusion. For family (iv), every edge of its Kan domain $K$ is an equivalence by [lem-coef-infinity-core-kan-fibration]. A simplicial map $K\to E$ preserves the two inverse-triangle witnesses, so these edges map to equivalences and hence to cartesian edges by the same relative outer-horn lemma. No base map $K\to S$ is assumed constant. Thus all four families lift. The lifting property is closed under pushouts by gluing a filler, under transfinite compositions by successive fillers and their union at limits, and under retracts by including and projecting a filler. It therefore holds for every marked-anodyne map.

source.place: Agent expansion of proof paragraph 2 through the finite-simplex terminal-comparison ancestry; marked lifting and terminal boundary extension, with all parameter boundaries fixed.

proof.text: Fix a parameter dimension $m\geq0$ and a boundary lifting problem for restriction. By the definition of the functor simplicial set this is a map on $(X\times\partial\Delta^m)\cup(B_n\times\Delta^m)$ with the prescribed diagonal and row conditions. Mark $Y_n$ by constant first coordinate and $D_n$ by restriction; mark the parameter simplex minimally. The marked product edges are exactly row edges at parameter vertices. By [lem-coef-triangular-top-deletion-anodyne], $D_n\hookrightarrow Y_n$ is marked anodyne. Its pushout product with $(\partial\Delta^m)^\flat\hookrightarrow(\Delta^m)^\flat$ is marked anodyne by [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus]. Step 2 lifts this map into $E^\natural$ over the fixed base map $\sigma\circ\operatorname{pr}_j$, ignoring the parameter. We obtain the extension on $Y_n\times\Delta^m$ preserving all required row edges and both prescribed restrictions. The diagonal strips there already belong to $D_n\times\Delta^m$ and remain fixed.

source.place: Agent expansion of proof paragraph 2 through the finite-simplex terminal-comparison ancestry; marked lifting and terminal boundary extension, with all parameter boundaries fixed.

proof.text: It remains to fill $C_n\times\Delta^m$, compatibly with its intersection with the map already defined. Its base projection is constant at $\sigma(n)$, so this is a problem in the strict fibre $E_n$, which is a quasicategory directly from innerness: an inner-horn square in the fibre lies over the constant simplex at $\sigma(n)$, and an inner-fibration filler stays in that fibre. The entire face opposite $(n,n)$ is already defined through $Y_n$. The strip $\{(n,n)\}\times\Delta^m$ is already constant at $t_n$, since $(n,n)\in B_n$. Order the remaining nondegenerate simplices of $C_n\times\Delta^m=N([n]\times[m])$ by dimension. Each has last column coordinate $n$: otherwise it would lie in the already defined opposite face. Its last vertex therefore maps to $t_n$. All its proper faces have been defined when it is attached. Apply [lem-cbc-terminal-boundary-extension] in $E_n$ to fill this whole boundary, leaving all previous simplices fixed; assign degenerate simplices by their operators. No missing vertex occurs, since every vertex is either in the opposite face or in the fixed strip. This finite induction fills the product. There is no new nondegenerate row edge in this last stage: an edge within the column has constant first coordinate only if it lies in a single-vertex parameter strip, and all such strips were already fixed or already defined. Thus the resulting map is an $m$-simplex of $\mathcal L(X)$ with the prescribed boundary and restriction.

source.place: Agent expansion of proof paragraph 2 through the finite-simplex terminal-comparison ancestry; marked lifting and terminal boundary extension, with all parameter boundaries fixed.

proof.text: Steps 3 and 4 solve every boundary lifting problem, including $m=0$ (where the parameter boundary is empty). By [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration] this proves that restriction is a trivial Kan fibration for every $n\geq1$. For $n=0$, $B_0$ is empty and the full diagram is required to be constant at $t_0$ in every parameter degree. Both simplicial sets are consequently the one-point simplicial set, and their restriction is an isomorphism.

source.place: Agent expansion of proof paragraph 2 through the finite-simplex terminal-comparison ancestry; marked lifting and terminal boundary extension, with all parameter boundaries fixed.

proof.text: We next show that the proper-face choice space maps to a point with every boundary lifting property, still in the generalized setting of step 1. Given $\partial\Delta^m\to\mathcal L(B_n)$, process the nonempty proper index subsets $F$ in increasing cardinality. At $N(T_F)$ the intersection with all previously processed nerves is exactly its own proper-face union $B_F$: intersections are the full nerve on the intersection of the index sets, and all proper subsets of $F$ were processed earlier. Keep the original parameter boundary as well. Order-identify $F$ with $[r]$, $r=|F|-1$, and apply step 5 to the same cartesian fibration $E\to S$ and the restricted simplex $N(F)^{\mathrm{op}}\to S$. Thus we use exactly the same cartesian edges in $E$; no reflection theorem for cartesian edges under pullback is needed. Its diagonal values are the already specified terminal objects in the same strict fibres. The extension agrees on intersections, so the maps glue. Singleton faces use the forced constant diagonal map. All proper faces have now been filled, giving the requested simplex of $\mathcal L(B_n)$. For $n=0$ this space is a point. The case $m=0$ supplies nonemptiness.

source.place: Agent expansion of proof paragraph 2 through the finite-simplex terminal-comparison ancestry; marked lifting and terminal boundary extension, with all parameter boundaries fixed.

proof.text: By steps 5 and 6 the map $\mathcal L(X)\to\Delta^0$ has the same boundary lifting property: first fill a parameter boundary in $\mathcal L(B_n)$, then lift the resulting simplex along restriction. Thus the maps from both spaces to a point are trivial Kan fibrations. By [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms] they lift horn inclusions as well, so both spaces are Kan; dimension-zero boundary lifting gives their vertices. For either map to a point, [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-homotopy-equivalence] gives a section and a simplicial homotopy between the identity and the constant map defined by that section. The map to a point is therefore a weak homotopy equivalence by [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak]. This is precisely contractibility in the convention of the statement.

source.place: Agent expansion of proof paragraph 2 through the finite-simplex terminal-comparison ancestry; marked lifting and terminal boundary extension, with all parameter boundaries fixed.

proof.text: For the last clause, let $p:E\to S$ be cartesian and form the actual degreewise pullback $E'=E\times_S N([n])^{\mathrm{op}}$. An inner-horn square for $E'\to N([n])^{\mathrm{op}}$ projects to one for $p$; pair its filler in $E$ with the prescribed base simplex to fill the original square. A $p$-cartesian lift of the image of any base edge, with the prescribed target, pairs with that edge to give a cartesian lift in $E'$: its final-horn fillers pair in the same manner. Thus the pullback is cartesian. Its total space is a quasicategory: fill the image of any inner horn in the ordinal nerve, then lift it by innerness. Its strict fibres identify degreewise with $E_{\sigma(i)}$, so their given terminal objects are still terminal. Apply steps 1 through 7 to this cartesian fibration over the ordinal nerve. No assertion that every cartesian edge of $E'$ is detected in $E$ is used. Terminality was used only within individual strict fibres, never after cartesian transport.
